title: Derivative of Gaussian noise along the exponential parameter
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure. Suppose that, as $u\to0^+$, the $L^2$ norm of $x\mapsto (f(x)-T_{e^{-u}}f(x))/u-g(x)$ tends to zero, where $T_\rho f(x)$ is the Gaussian average of $f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,Y)$ for a standard Gaussian vector $Y$. For every $t>0$ and $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the function $s\mapsto T_{e^{-s}}f(x)$ is differentiable at $t$, with derivative $-T_{e^{-t}}g(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ and $g$ are square-integrable under product standard Gaussian measure
The stated $L^2$ difference quotient tends to zero as $u\to0^+$
